analysis.title: Systematic Flows Monitor: Historic selloff takes US CTA equity longs to flat as vol control de-risks
key_insights: US CTA equity longs likely went to flat after Thursday's (5-Nov) post-election reversal, and faster models turned short across markets. CTAs had entered the week with US equity longs well below peak after October's selling.

The realized vol spike likely forced de-risking from both still-long CTAs and traditional vol control. BofA says that selling has likely run its course, leaving vol control exposure sharply reduced and US CTA books broadly flat.
Europe and Asia should lead any further CTA selling. Slightly long European positioning is at risk of flipping short, and Asian shorts are likely to extend.
Before Thursday, CTAs held more length in the S&P 500 than the Nasdaq-100, and Russell 2000 positioning was flat to slightly short.
CTAs remain stopped out of US Treasury and Bund shorts. Five consecutive weekly declines in 10yr yields have made futures trends less negative.
Trend followers are far from consensus long positions in bonds, but faster models could begin building longs if yields keep falling.
Korean Treasury bond futures positioning is mixed by model speed, but projections point to KTB buying next week. CTAs remain firmly long Chinese 10yr bond futures.
The dollar strengthened this week, leaving the EUR short as the most stretched FX position. Projections point to AUD selling and CAD buying next week.
The sharp decline in crude oil triggered some CTA long unwinds. Further weakness could bring more selling from CTAs that remain stretched long.

Gold shorts remain elevated, and the rebound has brought the first buy-to-cover triggers to roughly 2% above current levels. CTAs also stopped out of copper longs this week, and selling could broaden across the soybean complex next week.
SPX hedger gamma turned negative at -$4.9bn on 5-Nov, the lowest reading in the last year. BofA had flagged this possibility in the prior week's monitor.
SPX 5-day intraday realized vol rose to 17.9% as the SPX fell 4.36% and spot VIX rose nearly 12 points to 28 on 5-Nov. Gamma remains negative across a wide range around spot.
Longer-dated tenors (more than 1 month to expiry) contribute -$3.1bn of hedger gamma.
Leveraged and inverse ETF rebalancing amplified Thursday's selloff. BofA estimates US-domiciled funds sold $4bn of S&P 500 and $13bn of Nasdaq-100 exposure, which the report calls a record.

Systematic strategies could sell $37bn of global equities in a down market over the next week, stay firm if markets are flat, and buy $11bn in an up market. In a large down market CTAs would lead the selling, while in a median market vol control strategies could re-load.
Systematic global equity positioning across CTAs, risk parity and vol control is now above median levels relative to the last five years. Equity selling in bear paths would be led by Europe and Asia.

US leveraged and inverse ETFs would need to trade about $979mn of S&P 500 and $2.2bn of Nasdaq-100 per 1% move. That is $106mn and $263mn less than last week, and about 3% and 17% of the average 3:55-4:00 PM notional in ES and NQ futures plus QQQ.
Tesla and NVIDIA are the largest single-stock leveraged and inverse ETFs by AUM, at about $3.5bn and $3.2bn. Their rebalances are about $84mn (TSLA) and $73mn (NVDA) per 1% move.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Falling yields have made CTA bond futures trends less negative. Faster models could begin building longs if yields continue to fall.
The realized vol spike forced de-risking from CTAs and vol control.
Spot VIX jumped as the SPX fell 4.36% in one session.

risk_factors: Negative SPX gamma across a wide range around spot could amplify further moves.
Leveraged and inverse ETF end-of-day rebalancing can extend moves into the close.
European CTA longs could flip short and Asian shorts could extend if equities fall further.
Further crude oil weakness could bring more CTA long unwinds.
A large down market could bring $37bn of systematic selling over the next week, led by CTAs.

vol_and_positioning: SPX hedger gamma was -$4.9bn at the 5-Nov close, the lowest in a year. It remains negative in a wide range around spot.
Tenors beyond 1 month contribute -$3.1bn of hedger gamma.
Averaged intraday over the last 5 days, delta-hedgers were net short $2.6bn of SPX gamma: -$2.3bn from non-expiring options, -$3.3bn from 0DTEs and +$3.0bn from expiring open interest.
If delta-hedging were confined to the last 15 minutes of the session, SPX gamma may have been responsible for a 1.4pt (7%) decrease in S&P 500 e-mini realized vol over the past month.
US leveraged and inverse ETFs sold $4bn of S&P 500 and $13bn of Nasdaq-100 exposure on Thursday, which BofA estimates as a record.
Approximately $60bn of AUM sits in US S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 leveraged and inverse ETFs, over $100bn notional. AUM is about $21bn for the S&P 500 and $41bn for the Nasdaq-100.
Single-stock leveraged ETF AUM fell for most names this week, including TSLA (-$992mn), NVDA (-$703mn), MU (-$1,295mn) and SNDK (-$528mn).

CTA short-cover triggers: Russell 2000 at 2912 and Gold at 4154 (buy range 4154-4354). Long-unwind triggers: SX5E sell range 5946, Oil 87.0 to 84.1, Copper (BCOM) 621 to 593, Copper (GSCI) 13899 to 13469.
geopolitical: The report refers to a 'post-election reversal' on Thursday 5-Nov-2026 as the trigger for the equity selloff. It gives no further detail.
